rows: Measures the fine structure of the interplanetary magnetic field, mapped the Jovian magnetic field, and provides magnetic field measurements to evaluate solar wind interaction with Jupiter. [ 14 ] Principal investigator: Edward Smith / JPL Data: PDS/PPI data catalog, NSSDC data archive

Peer through a hole in the large dish-shaped antenna to detect particles of the solar wind originating from the Sun. [ 15 ] Principal investigator: Aaron Barnes / NASA Ames Research Center ( archived website ) [ 16 ] Data: PDS/PPI data catalog, NSSDC data archive
Detects cosmic rays in the Solar System. [ 17 ] Principal investigator: John Simpson / University of Chicago [ 16 ] Data: NSSDC data archive

Collects data on the composition of the cosmic ray particles and their energy ranges. [ 18 ] Principal investigator: Frank B. McDonald / NASA Goddard Space Flight Center [ 16 ] Data: PDS/PPI data catalog, NSSDC data archive

Surveys the intensities, energy spectra, and angular distributions of electrons and protons along the spacecraft's path through the radiation belts of Jupiter and Saturn. [ 19 ] Principal investigator: James A. Van Allen / University of Iowa ( website ) [ 16 ] Data: PDS/PPI data catalog, NSSDC data archive, NSSDC Jupiter data archive

Includes an unfocused Cerenkov counter that detects the light emitted in a particular direction as particles passed through it recording electrons of energy, 0.5 to 12 MeV, an electron scatter detector for electrons of energy, 100 to 400 keV, and a minimum ionizing detector consisting of a solid-state diode that measured minimum ionizing particles (<3 MeV) and protons in the range of 50 to 350 MeV. [ 20 ] Principal investigator: R. Fillius / University of California San Diego [ 16 ] Data: NSSDC hourly data archive, NSSDC Saturn data archive

Twelve panels of pressurized cell detectors mounted on the back of the main dish antenna record penetrating impacts of small meteoroids. [ 21 ] Principal investigator: William Kinard / NASA Langley Research Center [ 16 ] Data: NSSDC data archive list

Meteoroid-asteroid detector looks into space with four non-imaging telescopes to track particles ranging from close by bits of dust to distant large asteroids. [ 22 ] Principal investigator: Robert Soberman / General Electric Company [ 16 ] Data: NSSDC data archive list

Ultraviolet light (200 to 800 Å ) is sensed to determine the quantities of hydrogen and helium in space and on Jupiter and Saturn. [ 23 ] Principal investigator: Darrell Judge / University of Southern California [ 16 ] Data: PDS/PPI data catalog, NSSDC data archive

The imaging experiment relies upon the spin of the spacecraft to sweep a small telescope across the planet in narrow strips only 0.03 degrees wide, looking at the planet in red (5800 to 7000 Å ) and blue (3900 to 4900 Å) light. These strips are then processed to build up a visual image of the planet. [ 24 ] Principal investigator: Tom Gehrels / University of Arizona [ 16 ] Data: NSSDC data archive list
Provides information on cloud temperature and the output of heat from Jupiter and Saturn. [ 25 ] Principal investigator: Andrew Ingersoll / California Institute of Technology [ 16 ]

Measures the magnetic fields of both Jupiter and Saturn. This instrument is not carried on Pioneer 10. [ 26 ] Principal investigator: Mario Acuna / NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Data: NSSDC data archive list
